prompt: Up to what Largest Contentful Paint is a visit in the good band?
hint: The first row of the table.

choices.text: 2.5 seconds
choices.why: Right. Over 4 s is poor, and between the two needs improvement.

choices.text: 1 second
choices.why: Stricter than the published threshold; a page there is good with room to spare.

choices.text: 4 seconds
choices.why: That is where poor begins, not where good ends.

choices.text: 200 milliseconds
choices.why: That is the good threshold of INP, a different metric.

prompt: Why does Lighthouse report Total Blocking Time where the Core Web Vitals name INP?
hint: What does INP time, and who does it in a lab run?

choices.text: INP was retired in March 2024, and TBT took its place among the three vitals
choices.why: The other way round: INP replaced First Input Delay in March 2024.

choices.text: Nobody clicks or taps in a lab run, so there is no interaction to time
choices.why: Right. TBT measures the long tasks that would delay an interaction if there were one.

choices.text: TBT is the same metric under the name Lighthouse prefers
choices.why: They measure different things: blocked main-thread time against the delay of real interactions.

choices.text: INP is measured on the server, and Lighthouse runs inside a browser instead
choices.why: INP is measured in the visitor's browser, from their clicks and taps.

prompt: Match each metric to what it measures.
hint: The table and the paragraphs under the first figure.

pairs.right: when the largest element in view has been painted
how long an interaction waits for the next frame
how far visible content moves unasked
main-thread time lost to long tasks beyond 50 ms

right_distractors: how long the server took to send the first byte

prompt: When does a page meet the Core Web Vitals?

choices.text: When one Lighthouse run puts its score above 0.9
choices.why: The score is a lab summary; the vitals are judged on real visits.

choices.text: When the mean of its visits lands in the good band on each of the three
choices.why: A mean of a long tail describes nobody, which is why a percentile is used.

choices.text: When the 75th percentile of real visits is good on LCP, INP and CLS
choices.why: Right, with phones and desktops counted apart.

choices.text: When its slowest visit stays under the thresholds
choices.why: That would fail every page that has one visitor on a bad train connection.

prompt: Why is there no CrUX field data for the box office on your VM?

choices.text: CrUX is collected from real Chrome users of pages with enough traffic
choices.why: Right. A page nobody visits from the internet has no field data to collect.

choices.text: CrUX ignores pages served over plain HTTP
choices.why: The protocol is not the reason; the absence of visitors is.

choices.text: CrUX needs a script from Google installed on the page
choices.why: Chrome collects it from opted-in users without anything on the page.

choices.text: The VM's Chromium has usage statistics switched off
choices.why: Even with them on, one tester's visits are not a field.

prompt: What do the width and height attributes on the fixed page's buy?
hint: What the browser knows before the file arrives.

choices.text: A smaller file, because the browser then downloads fewer of the pixels
choices.why: The attributes change nothing about the file; hero-small.png is smaller for its own reasons.

choices.text: The picture's shape, so its space is reserved before it arrives
choices.why: Right. With height: auto the reserved box keeps the aspect ratio at any width.

choices.text: A higher priority for the download
choices.why: That is what fetchpriority="high" asks for.

choices.text: Lazy loading, so the picture waits until it is scrolled into view
choices.why: That would be loading="lazy", and the wrong choice for the largest element on screen.

prompt: What does a plain <script src> in the <head> do to the page while it loads and runs?
hint: The parser and the first paint.

choices.text: Nothing visible: scripts run after the page is drawn
choices.why: That is what defer arranges. A plain script stops the parser where it stands.

choices.text: It slows the download of the HTML
choices.why: The HTML has arrived; it is the parsing and painting that wait.

choices.text: The parser stops, and nothing is painted until it has finished
choices.why: Right. slow.js kept the screen blank for its 500 ms, four times longer on the simulated phone.

choices.text: It raises CLS, because the script moves content that was already on screen
choices.why: It delays the first paint; it moves nothing that was already drawn.

prompt: slow.js loops for 500 ms, and Lighthouse's long-tasks audit reported its task as 2,000 ms. By what factor did the simulated phone slow the processor?
Why is --no-sandbox acceptable for the Chromium that Lighthouse drives on the VM?
hint: What the browser opens, and where.

choices.text: Ubuntu 24.04 has its own sandbox that replaces Chromium's
choices.why: AppArmor's restriction is what stops Chromium building its sandbox; it is not a replacement.

choices.text: The sandbox protects a browser with a window, and this one has none
choices.why: Headless Chromium runs web pages just the same, and the sandbox protects against them.

choices.text: Lighthouse refuses to run while Chromium's sandbox is switched on
choices.why: Lighthouse does not care; Chromium refuses to start on Ubuntu 24.04 without it or the flag.

choices.text: It is a test browser that opens your own page on 127.0.0.1
choices.why: Right. It is still no way to browse the web.

prompt: In Lighthouse 13.5.0's performance score, which metric carries the largest weight?
hint: The weights block of the transcript.

choices.text: Largest Contentful Paint
choices.why: 25%, the same as CLS.

choices.text: Total Blocking Time
choices.why: Right, 30%.

choices.text: First Contentful Paint
choices.why: 10%, the same as Speed Index.

choices.text: Speed Index

prompt: Lighthouse is told where the browser lives through the environment variable ___.
What does Lighthouse's default throttling method, simulate, do?
hint: Is anything slowed while the page loads?

choices.text: Slows the browser's network and its processor for real while the page loads
choices.why: That is the devtools method.

choices.text: Loads at full speed, then computes how long a slow phone would have taken
choices.why: Right. That is why a 500 ms loop came back as 2,000 ms.

choices.text: Replays the page on a real phone that sits in one of Google's own laboratories
choices.why: Everything runs on your machine; no phone is involved.

choices.text: Applies nothing and reports what this machine did
choices.why: That is the provided method, which scored the slow page 0.9.

prompt: With --throttling-method=provided the slow page scored 0.9. What does that run tell you?
hint: Who visits a page over loopback?

choices.text: The default settings exaggerate, and 0.9 is closer to the truth
choices.why: Neither run is the truth; this one describes a visitor nobody has.

choices.text: The four defects matter on slow phones and not on desktops
choices.why: On a fast desktop on a good connection they cost less, and they still cost something.

choices.text: How the page behaves on this VM over 127.0.0.1, which describes no visitor
choices.why: Right. A 2.4 MB picture costs nothing over loopback.

choices.text: The page passes once the same files are served from a faster server than this one
choices.why: The server was the same in both runs; the throttling was what changed.

prompt: Which of these does WebPageTest give you that a Lighthouse run on your VM does not? Pick every one that applies.
hint: Real browsers, real places, and a view of the load as it happened.

choices.text: A filmstrip of the screen as the page loaded
choices.why: Right. Lighthouse reports numbers; the filmstrip shows the frames.

choices.text: A test from a device in another city
choices.why: Right. Its test agents run in real locations.

choices.text: A waterfall of requests, split into connection, waiting and download
choices.why: Right. It is the clearest view of a blocking script or a heavy file.

choices.text: INP measured from the visits of real customers
choices.why: That is field data. WebPageTest is a lab too, only a better-placed one.

choices.text: A test of a page that answers on 127.0.0.1 inside your VM
choices.why: WebPageTest runs on the internet and cannot reach a page on your VM.

prompt: Put these in the order they happen when Lighthouse loads the slow page.
hint: FCP was 2.8 s and LCP 13.1 s.
items: slow.js runs, and the screen stays blank
the heading is painted: First Contentful Paint
the heavy picture is painted: Largest Contentful Paint

prompt: Lighthouse in the pipeline reports an LCP of 1.9 s on the median of five runs, but field data puts the 75th percentile at 3.4 s. What follows?
hint: Which one does the requirement name?

choices.text: The requirement fails, and the lab's conditions do not match the visitors
choices.why: Right. The requirement is about real visits, and the lab is a proxy to correct.

choices.text: The lab is right, because five runs and a median beat noisy field data
choices.why: The median removes noise between lab runs; it cannot make the lab's phone a real one.

choices.text: The two average out to 2.65 s, close enough to the threshold
choices.why: They measure different things, and averaging them describes neither.

choices.text: The field data is stale, since CrUX covers 28 days
choices.why: Twenty-eight days of customers waiting 3.4 s is the finding, not a defect of it.

prompt: A change takes the slow page's TBT from 1,430 ms to 0 ms in the lab. What does that say about INP?
hint: What TBT measures, and what it leaves out.

choices.text: INP is now 0 ms as well, since the two of them measure exactly the same delay
choices.why: TBT says nothing about how long a click handler takes once it runs.

choices.text: No conclusion, because TBT and INP are unrelated and measure different moments of a visit
choices.why: They are related: long tasks during the load are what delay an early tap.

choices.text: Early taps stop waiting behind long tasks; slow handlers would still show in the field
choices.why: Right. The field, or the Performance panel with you clicking, is where INP is measured.

choices.text: INP passes, because Lighthouse scored the page 1 after the change
choices.why: The score summarises lab metrics, and INP is not one of them.
